content.text:
`vitest -p` is short for `--project`. It runs only the projects you name when your config defines several projects (Vitest's workspace feature). You can repeat it to pick more than one project, for example `-p app -p lib`. It also takes wildcards like `-p "packages*"` and exclusions like `-p "!e2e"`. A project runs if it matches none of the exclusions and, when you also give normal patterns, at least one of those.

I checked this in the installed vitest 5.0.3: its command-line definitions list `p` as the short form of `--project`. The project's Ludion notes say this shorthand was added in vitest 5.0.0, so older versions may not have it.
